oneliner.t: Republican former RNC chairman (2024–2025) and N.C. GOP chairman (2019–2024), a lawyer and former energy-industry lobbyist and Senate chief of staff, who won the March 3, 2026 primary with 64.6% on Trump's endorsement and is running for office for the first time.

born.t: October 7, 1968, Michigan (age 57 in March 2026 per AP, consistent)

hometown.t: Blowing Rock / Watauga County, North Carolina (moved there in early high school)

profile.residence: Gaston County, NC (Carolina Journal; AP's ballot listing gives Boone)

upbringing.t: Whatley was born in Michigan and moved to Watauga County in the North Carolina mountains during his early high-school years. His father was an accountant and his mother a librarian. As a sophomore at Watauga High School he volunteered on Jesse Helms's 1984 Senate re-election campaign, and he graduated in 1987. He earned a history degree from UNC Charlotte (1991), a master's in religion from Wake Forest (1993), and a master's in theology (1994) and law degree (1997) from Notre Dame. He lives in Gaston County with his wife, Suzanne, and their three children. NBC News reported that his Michigan roots largely drop out of his campaign biography.

education.school: University of North Carolina at Charlotte

career.role: Law clerk to U.S. District Judge Robert Potter
Member of George W. Bush's Florida recount team; senior official in the Bush-Cheney campaign
Chief of staff to Sen. Elizabeth Dole
Partner / co-founder, lobbying and PR firm representing oil and gas clients (Wikipedia dates partnership to 2007; Spectrum says he helped found it in 2009)

career.org: Consumer Energy Alliance (energy-industry group; funders include ExxonMobil and Chevron)

career.role: Helped organize Trump rallies in N.C.; helped lead Trump transition teams for energy, environment and agriculture
Chairman (with Lara Trump as co-chair); re-elected Jan 2025; stepped down to run for Senate
Member, appointed by Trump; also described as Trump's Helene 'recovery czar' for western N.C., a title his campaign has tried to disavow

platform.t: Campaign issues page: 'I am committed to advancing President Trump's America First agenda'; pledges to be Trump's ally in the Senate.
More police on the street with better pay, keep dangerous criminals in prison; proposes a federal version of 'Iryna's Law' limiting pretrial release for violent-offense defendants.
Supports the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act tax cuts, middle-class tax cuts and no tax on tips, overtime and Social Security; says waste, fraud and abuse should be cut from Medicaid and SNAP.
Defended the 2025 law's Medicaid cuts and favors market-driven replacements for the ACA.
Backs the federal Education Freedom Tax Credit; says 'dollars should follow students.'
'All of the above' energy; supports oil and gas leasing; criticized Obama-era EPA carbon rules as an industry lobbyist.
Would push to eliminate sanctuary cities; praised ICE's Charlotte operation as 'strong, decisive action'; attacks Cooper's ICE-cooperation vetoes.
Supports the Iran war ('we cannot allow Iran to have nuclear weapons') and continued military aid to Israel, which he calls the U.S.'s No. 1 ally in the Middle East.
Said in May 2026 he had suggested Trump abolish FEMA; prefers block grants to states for disaster relief.
NRA-endorsed; pledges to defend gun rights 'unapologetically.'
Led the state GOP's voter-ID push; as RNC chair touted 170+ election lawsuits; supports the SAVE America Act.
Campaign says he supports requiring elected officials to put assets in qualified blind trusts.

promises.t: Advance President Trump's America First agenda as his Senate ally.
Put more police on the street and pay them better; pass a federal Iryna's Law.
Lower taxes, including no tax on tips, overtime and Social Security.
Support requiring elected officials to use qualified blind trusts.

claims.claim: Has never run for office before (implicit in launch and AP coverage).

record.t: No prior candidacy for public office appears in Wikipedia or FEC records. Party chairmanships are internal party elections.

claims.claim: Running 'with the complete and total endorsement of President Trump.'

said.where: campaign launch speech, Loray Mill, Gastonia

record.t: Trump endorsed him on Truth Social before the launch.

claims.claim: Campaign bio: federal law clerk, a U.S. senator's chief of staff, and RNC chairman.

said.where: campaign website bio (as described by Spectrum News; site not reachable)

record.t: Clerked for U.S. District Judge Robert Potter, was Sen. Elizabeth Dole's chief of staff 2004–07, and was RNC chair March 2024–Aug. 2025. Spectrum notes the bio leaves out his more than a decade of oil-and-gas lobbying.

claims.claim: Raised in Blowing Rock, the son of a librarian and an accountant.

record.t: Moved to Watauga County in early high school (born in Michigan in 1968). Father an accountant, mother a librarian.

claims.claim: Roy Cooper 'bears direct responsibility' for the August 2025 Charlotte light-rail stabbing of Iryna Zarutska.

said.where: Whatley statements, Sept. 2025 (date/venue per WRAL fact check as summarized)

record.t: WRAL rated the claim False on Sept. 12, 2025. PolitiFact found no evidence the 2020 task force played a role in suspect DeCarlos Brown's release, and fact checks have repeatedly rejected tying Cooper's 2021 prison settlement to Brown. WRAL reported the settlement had no bearing on his case. (Fact checks are cited here as summarized by an NCDP release and a news report; the WRAL page was not opened directly.)

claims.claim: Cooper, through a 2021 COVID-era settlement, voluntarily released more than 4,200 violent criminals.

record.t: A Wake County judge issued a preliminary injunction in June 2020 and the state settled in February 2021. The settlement sped the transition of at least 3,500 people out of prison over six months. The releases followed litigation rather than being 'voluntary', and no source shows all of them were violent offenders.

claims.claim: On Harvey West Jr., a registered sex offender in state GOP roles: 'I did not hire the guy. Absolutely not.' (also told WITN he did not appoint West)

record.t: West was not a hire: his roles were volunteer party committee posts. District committee members elected him 1st District chair. But West says Whatley appointed him to the Plan of Organization Committee in 2021 and 2024, where he served under Whatley. The GOP says he simply kept serving, and WITN notes party rules give the chairman appointment power. Whatley's campaign declined PolitiFact's request for comment.

entries.t: Criticized Gov. Cooper for not doing enough to protect prisoners and corrections officers from COVID-19.
Attacks Cooper for the COVID-era prison settlement that sped releases.
Appointed to Trump's FEMA Review Council; campaign spokesperson said he supports making federal disaster management more efficient.
Said he had suggested the President abolish FEMA; prefers block grants to states.

aipac_endorse.t: Not confirmed. AIPAC's endorsement page and Track AIPAC could not be reached, and no AIPAC endorsement turned up in coverage reviewed (as of 2026-10-14).

aipac_pac.note: 2026 cycle — AIPAC PAC earmarks appear as individual contributions and were not checked; no AIPAC PAC committee contribution appears in FEC committee-contribution records

statements.t: Said the U.S. alliance with Israel is more than geopolitical; it is moral.

At a Republican Jewish Coalition event, called Israel the U.S.'s No. 1 ally in the Middle East, backed continued military aid and the Iran war, and attacked Cooper over a 2018 Iftar guest and campus Gaza protests.

fec.history_note: 2026 is his first candidacy. He also sponsors a leadership PAC, North Carolina First (C00914028). pac_biz/pac_ideo come from itemized FEC committee contributions through the records pull (2026-10-13), which runs past June 30. pac_biz = corporate $135,500 (e.g., Phillips 66 PAC $10,000) + trade $93,500 (ABC PAC, US Energy PAC $10,000 each). pac_ideo = leadership $502,000 + ideological $73,500 + membership $66,021 (incl. RJC-PAC) + super PAC/hybrid $25,000 + candidate committees $24,000. Lobbyist/registrant PACs gave $246,521. 'other' = transfers from authorized committees $4,621,452.36 + other receipts $177,107.10 + offsets $72,133.27.

note.t: As reported (Senate eFD not opened directly): his Senate financial disclosure shows more than $714,000 in 2024 income from party chairmanship and over $1M total 2024 income, plus stock in pharmaceutical, oil and technology companies (News & Observer, Feb. 12, 2026, via NCDP). Spectrum News reports his family holds hundreds of thousands of dollars in ExxonMobil and Chevron stock (both Consumer Energy Alliance funders) and Duke Energy shares. Carolina Public Press puts the Duke holding at $163,000–$445,000 (cited via NCDP, not opened). Cardinal & Pine, citing WUNC, reports Chemours gave his campaign $5,000.

revolving.role: Chief of staff to a senator, then energy-industry lobbyist
revolving.org: U.S. Senate (Sen. Elizabeth Dole) → HBW Resources / Consumer Energy Alliance
revolving.t: Left Sen. Dole's office in 2007 to lobby for oil and gas clients at HBW Resources and served as Consumer Energy Alliance EVP (2008–2019). Spectrum's review of 12 years of lobbying reports found $3.5M reported by Whatley and linked lobbyists, $1.2M from energy clients. Experts call his Senate bid a 'reverse revolving door'.

revolving.role: Energy Department official, then energy lobbyist
revolving.t: Deputy assistant secretary at DOE under President George W. Bush before his energy lobbying career (exact DOE dates not documented).

democracy.t: After the Jan. 6 Capitol attack, declined to blame Trump, saying only those who took part in the riot bear responsibility.

Said 'we certainly saw evidence of voting irregularities, of election counting irregularities in a number of places' around the country in 2020, and that Trump won N.C. because the state party was vigilant against Democratic attempts to cheat. CNN reported in 2024 that he promoted false election-fraud claims.
Said he approves of Trump's proposed $1.8 billion fund for supporters convicted of crimes, including Jan. 6 rioters.

townhalls.period: since the March 2026 primary: campaign says 100+ public events in all 100 counties, many organized by county GOPs (unverified; not formal town halls)

access.note: As of Sept. 10, 2026 neither nominee had accepted invitations from Spectrum News, the N.C. Association of Broadcasters or WUNC/UNC. Whatley said 'I'm happy to debate' but had not publicly called for one. His campaign limited access for The Assembly and the Asheville Citizen-Times, and he sometimes leaves events without taking questions.

note.t: Born in Michigan in 1968 and moved to Watauga County in early high school (about the mid-1980s). He studied at Notre Dame (to 1997) and worked in Washington for the Energy Department and the Senate (2004–07). The years spent outside North Carolina can't be totaled from the record, so no figure is given.

checks.legal: Courts: CourtListener and Justia direct searches were blocked for this research tool. Wikipedia lists no lawsuits against him, and none turned up in the 2025–26 coverage reviewed (PolitiFact/WRAL, Spectrum, Daily Beast, WSPA, AP). Party-capacity litigation as RNC chair is not counted. Ethics: no congressional or state ethics body has jurisdiction (never held elected office). His party roles were reviewed via PolitiFact's Harvey West fact check.
checks.foreign: FARA bulk-file exact-name check (2026-10-13): no row names Michael Whatley (0 name matches). His lobbying for energy clients was domestic per Spectrum, and no foreign principal turned up. Senate financial disclosure was not opened directly (reported contents show U.S. stocks only).
checks.claims: v2.1 mechanical sample NOT possible: michaelwhatley.com (bio and /issues/) could not be opened (fetch blocked by provenance rule; the site never appeared in search results). Ad spend and specific ads were not identified. Instead used his own claims as reported by news: launch-speech claims (2025-07-31), the campaign-site bio as described by Spectrum, and his most-covered attack lines on Cooper (Charlotte stabbing; prison settlement) and his Harvey West denial. 7 checkable claims were rated. This is less mechanical than Cooper's sample (his About page was opened directly).
checks.democracy: Never in Congress, so no certification votes (records pull read 6 roll calls; none apply). His public statements on 2020 come from Wikipedia (citing his Feb. 2021 remarks and a 2024 CNN report) and OnTheIssues. His Jan. 6 fund position comes from Cardinal & Pine citing WRAL.

recordx.note: missed_pct does not apply (never in Congress). The FEC committee page for C00913996 lists no RFAIs, but its notices section did not render, so 'clean' is not confirmed. Senate candidate disclosure timeliness was not checked. Fewer than two record items are documented.

corp.t: Took business PAC money in 2026: corporate PACs $135,500 (incl. Phillips 66 PAC $10,000; Chemours $5,000 per WUNC) and trade-association PACs $93,500 (ABC PAC and US Energy PAC $10,000 each); ABC PAC also spent $45,550 independently for him. Lobbyist/registrant PACs gave $246,521.

lobby.t: Took $30,021 from the Republican Jewish Coalition PAC (10 contributions) in 2026.

research_notes: MONEY: FEC candidate page S6NC00415 opened directly (through 2026-06-30). The Q3 2026 report was not yet shown. Track AIPAC and super PAC donor lists (AFP Action, No Going Back PAC, SLF PAC, WinSenate) were not checked. NRSC coordinated expenditures ($7,964,365, Aug 2026) are listed as party support. The Assembly reported Whatley defended $350,000 from donor John Childs (charged in 2019, not convicted). That source was not opened, and it was unclear which committee got the money, so it is omitted from money2. DISPUTED FACTS: whether he 'appointed' Harvey West (rated partly); his HBW start year (2007 per Wikipedia vs. 2009 per Spectrum); RNC 'co-chair' vs 'chair' wording in Carolina Journal (Wikipedia and NC Newsline say chair); residence (Gaston County per Carolina Journal, Boone per AP ballot listing). The Daily Beast says he appointed West during his RNC tenure, which conflicts with PolitiFact's account, so PolitiFact is used. office_years left null: his DOE deputy assistant secretary dates are undocumented, and the FEMA Review Council is an advisory appointment. ACCESS: the campaign site, Ballotpedia, CourtListener, Track AIPAC, the Senate eFD and some WRAL pages were blocked for this tool, and the 12-search budget was used up. NEEDS HUMAN CHECK: michaelwhatley.com bio and first 10 issue claims; two top ads; Senate eFD report (net worth, Duke/Exxon/Chevron holdings, any trades); DOE service dates; super PAC funders.
